Gene Description

PPP1CA encodes PP1-alpha, one of three catalytic subunits (with PP1-beta and PP1-gamma) of protein phosphatase 1, a PPP-family metallo-phosphatase with a binuclear Fe/Zn (Mn in vitro) active site that hydrolyses phosphoserine and phosphothreonine on proteins. The catalytic subunit has little intrinsic substrate selectivity; it acts almost entirely as part of holoenzymes formed with more than 200 regulatory, targeting and inhibitor subunits, most of which dock on the RVxF-binding groove and direct PP1 to particular locations and substrates. PP1-alpha is predominantly nucleoplasmic but shuttles to the cytoplasm. Well-characterised holoenzymes include PNUTS-TOX4-WDR82-PP1, which dephosphorylates CDK9, MEPCE, SPT5, SPT6 and the RNA polymerase II CTD to promote promoter-proximal pause release, set elongation rate and drive poly(A)-coupled termination; the SHOC2-MRAS-PP1C holophosphatase, which removes the inhibitory 14-3-3-site phosphate of RAF kinases to activate RAS-MAPK signalling; GADD34/CReP-PP1, which dephosphorylates eIF2alpha to end the integrated stress response; glycogen-targeted PP1 in glycogen metabolism; and mitotic-exit and kinetochore holoenzymes (Repo-Man, Sds22). Other reported substrates include NBS1 (telomere repair choice), MYC, axin, PER proteins (circadian period), RIG-I/MDA5 and ATG16L1.

The PNUTS phosphatase complex controls transcription pause r... 		ACCEPT
Summary: PNUTS-PP1 promotes RNAPII pause release / transition into productive elongation.
Reason: Within PNUTS-PP1, PPP1CA dephosphorylates CDK9, MEPCE, NCBP1, SUPT6H and other pausing regulators, promoting release of promoter-proximally paused RNAPII. Summary: Bare protein-binding annotation from an interaction assay (IPI/IDA). PP1-alpha binds more than 200 regulatory, targeting and inhibitor subunits (most via RVxF-type short linear motifs) and many substrates and viral proteins; this row records one such interaction.
Reason: Per the protein-binding policy, GO:0005515 carries no functional information. Removal does not dispute the reported interaction. For PP1-alpha the informative content of these interactions is already captured by the catalytic activity (GO:0004722) and by membership of specific holoenzyme complexes (GO:0000164 protein phosphatase type 1 complex, GO:0072357 PTW/PP1 phosphatase complex); the catalytic subunit is the bound partner, so no regulator-side MF (e.g. phosphatase regulator activity) applies to PPP1CA itself.

Summary: Bare protein-binding annotation from an interaction assay (IPI/IDA). PP1-alpha binds more than 200 regulatory, targeting and inhibitor subunits (most via RVxF-type short linear motifs) and many substrates and viral proteins; this row records one such interaction.
Reason: Per the protein-binding policy, GO:0005515 carries no functional information. Removal does not dispute the reported interaction. For PP1-alpha the informative content of these interactions is already captured by the catalytic activity (GO:0004722) and by membership of specific holoenzyme complexes (GO:0000164 protein phosphatase type 1 complex, GO:0072357 PTW/PP1 phosphatase complex); the catalytic subunit is the bound partner, so no regulator-side MF (e.g. phosphatase regulator activity) applies to PPP1CA itself.

Docking motif-guided mapping of the interactome of protein p... 		REMOVE
Summary: Bare protein-binding annotation from an interaction assay (IPI/IDA). PP1-alpha binds more than 200 regulatory, targeting and inhibitor subunits (most via RVxF-type short linear motifs) and many substrates and viral proteins; this row records one such interaction.
Reason: Per the protein-binding policy, GO:0005515 carries no functional information. Removal does not dispute the reported interaction. For PP1-alpha the informative content of these interactions is already captured by the catalytic activity (GO:0004722) and by membership of specific holoenzyme complexes (GO:0000164 protein phosphatase type 1 complex, GO:0072357 PTW/PP1 phosphatase complex); the catalytic subunit is the bound partner, so no regulator-side MF (e.g. phosphatase regulator activity) applies to PPP1CA itself.

For PP1-alpha the informative content of these interactions is already captured by the catalytic activity (GO:0004722) and by membership of specific holoenzyme complexes (GO:0000164 protein phosphatase type 1 complex, GO:0072357 PTW/PP1 phosphatase complex); the catalytic subunit is the bound partner, so no regulator-side MF (e.g. phosphatase regulator activity) applies to PPP1CA itself.

An organelle-specific protein landscape identifies novel dis... 		REMOVE
Summary: Bare protein-binding annotation from an interaction assay (IPI/IDA). PP1-alpha binds more than 200 regulatory, targeting and inhibitor subunits (most via RVxF-type short linear motifs) and many substrates and viral proteins; this row records one such interaction.
Reason: Per the protein-binding policy, GO:0005515 carries no functional information. Removal does not dispute the reported interaction. For PP1-alpha the informative content of these interactions is already captured by the catalytic activity (GO:0004722) and by membership of specific holoenzyme complexes (GO:0000164 protein phosphatase type 1 complex, GO:0072357 PTW/PP1 phosphatase complex); the catalytic subunit is the bound partner, so no regulator-side MF (e.g. phosphatase regulator activity) applies to PPP1CA itself.

Summary: Bare protein-binding annotation from an interaction assay (IPI/IDA). PP1-alpha binds more than 200 regulatory, targeting and inhibitor subunits (most via RVxF-type short linear motifs) and many substrates and viral proteins; this row records one such interaction.
Reason: Per the protein-binding policy, GO:0005515 carries no functional information. Removal does not dispute the reported interaction. For PP1-alpha the informative content of these interactions is already captured by the catalytic activity (GO:0004722) and by membership of specific holoenzyme complexes (GO:0000164 protein phosphatase type 1 complex, GO:0072357 PTW/PP1 phosphatase complex); the catalytic subunit is the bound partner, so no regulator-side MF (e.g. phosphatase regulator activity) applies to PPP1CA itself.

Summary: Bare protein-binding annotation from an interaction assay (IPI/IDA). PP1-alpha binds more than 200 regulatory, targeting and inhibitor subunits (most via RVxF-type short linear motifs) and many substrates and viral proteins; this row records one such interaction.
Reason: Per the protein-binding policy, GO:0005515 carries no functional information. Removal does not dispute the reported interaction. For PP1-alpha the informative content of these interactions is already captured by the catalytic activity (GO:0004722) and by membership of specific holoenzyme complexes (GO:0000164 protein phosphatase type 1 complex, GO:0072357 PTW/PP1 phosphatase complex); the catalytic subunit is the bound partner, so no regulator-side MF (e.g. phosphatase regulator activity) applies to PPP1CA itself.

protein serine/threonine phosphatase activity

protein dephosphorylation

nucleoplasm cytoplasm

protein phosphatase type 1 complex

In the PNUTS-TOX4-WDR82-PP1 complex, dephosphorylates RNA polymerase II machinery (CDK9, MEPCE, NCBP1, SUPT6H, SPT5, CTD Ser5) to promote pause release and productive elongation and, downstream of poly(A) sites, to slow RNAPII for termination.

In the SHOC2-MRAS-PP1C holophosphatase, dephosphorylates the inhibitory 14-3-3-binding site of RAF kinases (CRAF S259, BRAF S365, ARAF S214), releasing autoinhibition and promoting RAS-MAPK signalling.

    Finally, the SMP holophosphatase complex dephosphorylates RAF at the ‘S259’ position, inducing RAF release from its autoinhibited state when bound to 14-3-31.

With PPP1R15A (GADD34) or PPP1R15B (CReP), dephosphorylates eIF2alpha Ser51 to restore translation initiation after the integrated stress response.

Suggested Questions for Experts

Q: Which PP1 holoenzymes depend specifically on the alpha isoform rather than PP1-beta or PP1-gamma, given >90% identity and largely shared regulatory subunits? Many process annotations (circadian, Wnt, photoperiod entrainment) rest on pan-PP1 inhibitors and may not be isoform-specific.

Q: Should GO provide a term for RNA polymerase II promoter-proximal pause release, so that PNUTS-PP1 annotations need not use promoter clearance?

Suggested Experiments

Experiment: Isoform-selective degron knock-in (PPP1CA vs PPP1CB/PPP1CC) with phosphoproteomics to define alpha-specific substrates and test which holoenzyme functions (PNUTS-PP1, SMP, GADD34-PP1) require PP1-alpha in vivo.

📚 Additional Documentation

Notes

(PPP1CA-notes.md)

PPP1CA notes

Literature search (no deep-research provider available)

Sources checked: the UniProt record P62136 (CC FUNCTION, SUBUNIT, SUBCELLULAR LOCATION), and every publication behind the GOA rows, cached by just fetch-gene-pmids human PPP1CA (82 papers). Full text was available for the SHOC2-MRAS-PP1C structure papers, the PNUTS pause-release (mouse) and termination papers, the NBS1 telomere paper, the MYC/PNUTS paper, the iron-PP1 paper, RIG-I/MDA5, Nox4/GADD34, E-cadherin BioID, Sds22/Repo-Man and the circadian paper. Several others were abstract-only (noted in each row's summary). Context only: the integrated stress response and telomere end-joining pathway-choice modules (proposed in ai4curation/ai-gene-review#5904).

Key findings

  • Catalytic subunit with no intrinsic selectivity: PMID:35768504
  • SMP complex: PMID:35830882
  • PNUTS-PP1 and pause release: PMID:39603240
  • PNUTS-PP1 and termination: PMID:31677974
  • PTW/PP1 complex: PMID:20516061
  • eIF2alpha phosphatase: PMID:26095357
  • NBS1 at telomeres: PMID:28216226
  • Location: PMID:17965019
  • Metal: PMID:30403291

Curation decisions

  • All 225 bare GO:0005515 rows: REMOVE, per the protein-binding policy. The interactions are mostly with regulatory subunits; their content is captured by the PP1 complex and PTW/PP1 complex CC rows.
  • phosphatase activity / phosphoprotein phosphatase activity: MODIFY to GO:0004722.
  • regulation of translational initiation in response to stress: MODIFY to GO:0036496 (eIF2alpha dephosphorylation), the term that names the PP1-catalysed step.
  • Glycogen, synaptic and circadian rows (mostly rodent transfers): KEEP_AS_NON_CORE as holoenzyme- or tissue-specific roles.
  • Photoperiod entrainment, response to lead, exosome, cadherin binding/cell-cell adhesion, PP1 binding, RNP/complex binding: MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED.
  • Cited TAS PMID:10640627 is about PP2A/PP2B rather than PP1. The activity row is accepted on other evidence.

id: P62136
gene_symbol: PPP1CA
product_type: PROTEIN
status: COMPLETE
taxon:
  id: NCBITaxon:9606
  label: Homo sapiens
description: PPP1CA encodes PP1-alpha, one of three catalytic subunits (with PP1-beta and PP1-gamma) of
  protein phosphatase 1, a PPP-family metallo-phosphatase with a binuclear Fe/Zn (Mn in vitro) active
  site that hydrolyses phosphoserine and phosphothreonine on proteins. The catalytic subunit has little
  intrinsic substrate selectivity; it acts almost entirely as part of holoenzymes formed with more than
  200 regulatory, targeting and inhibitor subunits, most of which dock on the RVxF-binding groove and
  direct PP1 to particular locations and substrates. PP1-alpha is predominantly nucleoplasmic but shuttles
  to the cytoplasm. Well-characterised holoenzymes include PNUTS-TOX4-WDR82-PP1, which dephosphorylates
  CDK9, MEPCE, SPT5, SPT6 and the RNA polymerase II CTD to promote promoter-proximal pause release, set
  elongation rate and drive poly(A)-coupled termination; the SHOC2-MRAS-PP1C holophosphatase, which removes
  the inhibitory 14-3-3-site phosphate of RAF kinases to activate RAS-MAPK signalling; GADD34/CReP-PP1,
  which dephosphorylates eIF2alpha to end the integrated stress response; glycogen-targeted PP1 in glycogen
  metabolism; and mitotic-exit and kinetochore holoenzymes (Repo-Man, Sds22). Other reported substrates
  include NBS1 (telomere repair choice), MYC, axin, PER proteins (circadian period), RIG-I/MDA5 and ATG16L1.

  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:

  review:
    summary: Bare protein-binding annotation from an interaction assay (IPI/IDA). PP1-alpha binds more
      than 200 regulatory, targeting and inhibitor subunits (most via RVxF-type short linear motifs) and
      many substrates and viral proteins; this row records one such interaction.
    action: REMOVE
    reason: Per the protein-binding policy, GO:0005515 carries no functional information. Removal does
      not dispute the reported interaction. For PP1-alpha the informative content of these interactions
      is already captured by the catalytic activity (GO:0004722) and by membership of specific holoenzyme
      complexes (GO:0000164 protein phosphatase type 1 complex, GO:0072357 PTW/PP1 phosphatase complex);
      the catalytic subunit is the bound partner, so no regulator-side MF (e.g. phosphatase regulator
      activity) applies to PPP1CA itself.

      many substrates and viral proteins; this row records one such interaction.
    action: REMOVE
    reason: Per the protein-binding policy, GO:0005515 carries no functional information. Removal does
      not dispute the reported interaction. For PP1-alpha the informative content of these interactions
      is already captured by the catalytic activity (GO:0004722) and by membership of specific holoenzyme
      complexes (GO:0000164 protein phosphatase type 1 complex, GO:0072357 PTW/PP1 phosphatase complex);
      the catalytic subunit is the bound partner, so no regulator-side MF (e.g. phosphatase regulator
      activity) applies to PPP1CA itself.
    supported_by: *id003

- term:

    label: nucleus
  evidence_type: EXP
  original_reference_id: PMID:17965019
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: Localization of PP1-alpha in interphase nuclei.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: PP1-alpha is predominantly nuclear (nucleoplasm and nuclear speckles, excluded from nucleoli)
      and acts there on transcription, chromatin and mitotic-exit substrates. Nucleus is not covered by
      the root-organelle policy, but is an informative location here and is complemented by accepted nucleoplasm
      rows.
    supported_by:
    - &id004
      reference_id: PMID:17965019
      supporting_text: PP1alpha is primarily nuclear and largely excluded from nucleoli

- term:
    id: GO:0034244
    label: negative regulation of transcription elongation by RNA polymerase II
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:31677974
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: PNUTS-PP1 slows RNAPII elongation after poly(A) sites.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: PNUTS-PP1 dephosphorylates SPT5 downstream of poly(A) sites, slowing RNAPII so the XRN2 torpedo
      can catch it (the "sitting duck" mechanism). This is the negative-regulation side of the same enzyme;
      it acts in a different gene region from pause release, so it does not conflict with the positive-regulation
      rows.
    supported_by:
    - &id014
      reference_id: PMID:31677974
      supporting_text: We report that PNUTS-PP1 phosphatase is a negative regulator of RNA polymerase
        II (Pol II) elongation rate.
    - reference_id: PMID:31677974
      supporting_text: Immediately downstream of poly(A) sites, Pol II decelerates from >2 kb/min to <1
        kb/min, which correlates with Spt5 dephosphorylation.

    label: RNA polymerase II CTD heptapeptide repeat S5 phosphatase activity
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:33264625
  qualifier: enables
  review:
    summary: PNUTS-PP1 dephosphorylates RNAPII CTD Ser5 (abstract-only paper).
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: UniProt (curated from this paper) records PNUTS-PP1 dephosphorylation of POLR2A CTD Ser5,
      promoting RNAPII turnover on chromatin during replication stress. A specific substrate-defined child
      of GO:0004722, exercised in the PNUTS holoenzyme.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:33264625
      supporting_text: WDR82 also promotes RNAPII-CTD dephosphorylation and suppresses replication stress
    - reference_id: file:human/PPP1CA/PPP1CA-uniprot.txt
      record_section:
      - CC:FUNCTION
      supporting_text: PNUTS-PP1 complex is also involved in the response to replication stress by mediating
        dephosphorylation of POLR2A at 'Ser-5' of the CTD
- term:
    id: GO:2000806
    label: positive regulation of termination of RNA polymerase II transcription, poly(A)-coupled
  evidence_type: IDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:31677974
  qualifier: involved_in
  review:
    summary: PNUTS-PP1 promotes poly(A)-coupled termination.
    action: ACCEPT
    reason: PNUTS-PP1 dephosphorylates SPT5 downstream of poly(A) sites, slowing RNAPII so the XRN2 torpedo
      can catch it (the "sitting duck" mechanism).
    supported_by:
    - *id014
    - reference_id: file:human/PPP1CA/PPP1CA-uniprot.txt
      record_section:
      - CC:FUNCTION
      supporting_text: The PNUTS-PP1 complex also regulates transcription termination by mediating dephosphorylation
        of SUPT5H in termination zones downstream of poly(A) sites

core_functions:
- description: 'Catalytic subunit of protein phosphatase 1 holoenzymes: hydrolyses phosphoserine/phosphothreonine
    on substrate proteins chosen by the bound regulatory subunit.'
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0004722
    label: protein serine/threonine phosphatase activity
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0006470
    label: protein dephosphorylation
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005654
    label: nucleoplasm
  - id: GO:0005737
    label: cytoplasm
  in_complex:
    id: GO:0000164
    label: protein phosphatase type 1 complex
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: file:human/PPP1CA/PPP1CA-uniprot.txt
    record_section:
    - CC:FUNCTION
    supporting_text: Protein phosphatase that associates with over 200 regulatory proteins to form highly
      specific holoenzymes which dephosphorylate hundreds of biological targets
  - reference_id: PMID:35768504
    supporting_text: although PP1C in isolation lacks intrinsic substrate selectivity
- description: In the PNUTS-TOX4-WDR82-PP1 complex, dephosphorylates RNA polymerase II machinery (CDK9,
    MEPCE, NCBP1, SUPT6H, SPT5, CTD Ser5) to promote pause release and productive elongation and, downstream
    of poly(A) sites, to slow RNAPII for termination.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0004722
    label: protein serine/threonine phosphatase activity
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0032968
    label: positive regulation of transcription elongation by RNA polymerase II
  - id: GO:2000806
    label: positive regulation of termination of RNA polymerase II transcription, poly(A)-coupled
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005654
    label: nucleoplasm
  in_complex:
    id: GO:0072357
    label: PTW/PP1 phosphatase complex
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:39603240
    supporting_text: PNUTS-PP1 promotes pause release by dephosphorylating multiple substrates, including
      the 7SK small nuclear ribonucleoprotein particle (snRNP) subunit MEPCE
  - reference_id: PMID:31677974
    supporting_text: Disruption of the PNUTS-PP1complex accelerated elongation in both gene bodies and
      3’ flanking regions and prevented efficient transcription termination.
- description: In the SHOC2-MRAS-PP1C holophosphatase, dephosphorylates the inhibitory 14-3-3-binding
    site of RAF kinases (CRAF S259, BRAF S365, ARAF S214), releasing autoinhibition and promoting RAS-MAPK
    signalling.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0004722
    label: protein serine/threonine phosphatase activity
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0046579
    label: positive regulation of Ras protein signal transduction
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005737
    label: cytoplasm
  in_complex:
    id: GO:0000164
    label: protein phosphatase type 1 complex
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:35831509
    supporting_text: Finally, the SMP holophosphatase complex dephosphorylates RAF at the ‘S259’ position,
      inducing RAF release from its autoinhibited state when bound to 14-3-31.
- description: With PPP1R15A (GADD34) or PPP1R15B (CReP), dephosphorylates eIF2alpha Ser51 to restore
    translation initiation after the integrated stress response.
  molecular_function:
    id: GO:0004722
    label: protein serine/threonine phosphatase activity
  directly_involved_in:
  - id: GO:0036496
    label: regulation of translational initiation by eIF2 alpha dephosphorylation
  locations:
  - id: GO:0005829
    label: cytosol
  in_complex:
    id: GO:0000164
    label: protein phosphatase type 1 complex
  supported_by:
  - reference_id: PMID:26095357
    supporting_text: Here, we report detailed structural and functional analyses of the GADD34:PP1 holoenzyme
      and its recruitment of eIF2α.
  - reference_id: file:human/PPP1CA/PPP1CA-uniprot.txt
    record_section:
    - CC:SUBUNIT
    supporting_text: Interacts with PPP1R15A and PPP1R15B; the interactions mediate binding to EIF2S1
suggested_questions:
- question: Which PP1 holoenzymes depend specifically on the alpha isoform rather than PP1-beta or PP1-gamma,
    given >90% identity and largely shared regulatory subunits? Many process annotations (circadian, Wnt,
    photoperiod entrainment) rest on pan-PP1 inhibitors and may not be isoform-specific.
- question: Should GO provide a term for RNA polymerase II promoter-proximal pause release, so that PNUTS-PP1
    annotations need not use promoter clearance?
suggested_experiments:
- description: Isoform-selective degron knock-in (PPP1CA vs PPP1CB/PPP1CC) with phosphoproteomics to define
    alpha-specific substrates and test which holoenzyme functions (PNUTS-PP1, SMP, GADD34-PP1) require
    PP1-alpha in vivo.
